prompts.text: What's the funniest way one of our friends has tried to introduce their partner to the group?
Recall a first meeting with a friend's partner that quickly became a warm memory.
Meet a friend's new partner over dinner or during a casual group activity?
Your friend brings somebody new to game night and they don't understand the running jokes. How would you include them?
A person's friendships often change shape when they begin a serious relationship.
A good group makes room for new partners without requiring everyone to become instantly close.
Which shared hobby would help a friend's new partner feel welcome in the group?
Describe a time a friend's partner introduced an unexpectedly fun tradition.
Our friend wants to organise a small gathering for their partner, who dislikes surprises. What might work?
A thoughtful welcome note or a relaxed activity without formal introductions?
Which friend always seems to know when someone needs cheering up?
Tell us about a small supportive gesture that brought the group closer.
Offer a helpful errand or arrange a light-hearted afternoon together?
One of our friends is coping with an exhausting week and wants company without conversation. What would we suggest?
A familiar friendship sometimes feels most comfortable when nobody expects entertainment.
Being reliable doesn't require solving everybody's problems.
What's one gesture that says someone understands how you handle stress?
Recall a friend quietly adjusting plans to make a difficult day easier.
A friend declines our plans several times in a row. How might we check in without making them defensive?
A short encouraging message or an offer to help with a practical task?
Who in our circle gives advice that starts seriously and ends with an unexpected joke?
Tell us about advice from a friend that sounded silly until it proved useful.
Ask for a friend's first instinct or request their detailed reasoning?
One friend wants a second opinion about a tricky social invitation. How would you help them weigh it?
People offer advice based partly on what worked for them, even when circumstances differ.
The most useful advice sometimes ends with asking what the person already wants.
What question has a friend asked that helped you reach your own decision?
Recall someone respectfully disagreeing with your choice and supporting you afterwards.
Our friend is torn between attending two important events. What's a fair way to discuss the options?
Get feedback from one trusted friend or hear several different viewpoints?
What's the most unexpected common interest you've had with a friend's relative?
Tell us about a friend's family welcoming you as though you'd known them for years.
Learn a recipe from a friend's parent or hear their funniest story from school days?
You attend a friend's family celebration and don't recognise anyone. What's a comfortable way to start chatting?
Friendships sometimes bring people into family traditions they never grew up with.
Being a guest works better when you're interested in the occasion rather than trying to impress everyone.
Which family tradition have you enjoyed because a friend introduced you to it?
Recall a time a friend's sibling revealed an unexpected side of their personality.
Our friend invites the group to an unfamiliar ceremony. What should we ask before attending?
Join a friend's holiday meal or attend their favourite annual community event?
Which friend is most likely to notice a change in your usual routine?
Recall someone asking an unusually specific question because they'd been paying attention.
Have friends remember your usual order or your favourite way to spend a free afternoon?
Your closest friends create a quiz about your tastes, but you get half the answers wrong. What might surprise you?
People sometimes remember the habits they see in a friend better than the friend does.
Remembering somebody's boundaries is more meaningful than memorising every favourite.
What's a harmless detail about you that your friends remember better than you do?
Describe the time a friend predicted your reaction with uncanny accuracy.
We each submit one question to a quiz about our friendship group. What would yours test?
Guess everyone's hidden talents or test how well we know their favourite places?
What's the most absurd reason your group has ever nearly cancelled an outing?
Tell us about a last-minute change that turned a dull gathering into a great memory.
Let the most organised friend plan the whole day or let everyone choose one stop?
One friend wants adventure, another wants quiet, and the others want food. What itinerary would make everyone smile?
Successful gatherings often involve small adjustments nobody announces.
The best group organisers leave space for different energy levels.
Who among our friends is best at spotting an easy compromise?
Recall a friend proposing an alternative that everyone liked more than the original plan.
Our group has a tiny outing budget and wildly different ideas. What would you ask everyone to prioritise?
Repeat an outing that worked brilliantly or risk trying a new activity together?
Which pair of friends have completely different personalities but get along brilliantly?
Tell us about two people who became close after initially disagreeing about everything.
Have a friend who shares your humour or one who introduces you to unfamiliar interests?
Two friends have opposite opinions about the same film. What question would get them talking rather than arguing?
Difference in temperament sometimes makes a friendship easier because people contribute different strengths.
You don't need identical personalities to care about the same values.
What difference between you and a friend has become something you appreciate?
Recall a friendship teaching you to be more patient with a different communication style.
A friend who loves planning joins forces with one who improvises. How would you divide their tasks?
A patient listener who loves details or a lively storyteller who keeps things moving?
What's an unexpected sign that two people are comfortable around each other?
Describe a conversation that became funny because neither person felt the need to act impressive.
Share comfortable silence with friends or exchange short stories over tea?
Two close friends decide to spend an afternoon together without screens. How would they keep it relaxed?
Close friends sometimes communicate whole reactions with a look across the room.
A relationship feels easier when people stop interpreting every quiet moment as a problem.
Which shared look or gesture has become a joke among your friends?
Recall an occasion when a friend knew what you meant before you'd finished explaining.
We try to communicate an ordinary message across a room without speaking. Who would be best at it?
A friendship that thrives on conversation or one that thrives on shared activities?
What's one friendship expectation you've outgrown without realising?
Tell us about reconnecting with someone and discovering your routines had changed.
Meet an old friend for a familiar meal or show them a new part of your life?
A friend moves away and your group starts missing their usual contributions. What new tradition would include them?
People adapt their friendships as their responsibilities and priorities shift.
A meaningful friendship doesn't require somebody to remain the same person you met years ago.
What's a change in a friend's life that made you admire them more?
Recall a reunion where a friend surprised you with a new hobby or ambition.
Our friend returns after living elsewhere for years. How might we welcome them without treating them like their old self?
Trade stories about how we've changed or revisit a favourite shared memory?
What's a harmless topic our friendship group debates far more often than necessary?
Tell us about the time a casual disagreement turned into a recurring group joke.
Create an annual silly debate night or a friendly award show about everybody's quirks?
We have to name one friendly rule for keeping disagreements playful. What would it be?
Long friendships accumulate funny disagreements that aren't serious enough to resolve.
Knowing when a joke has run its course is a friendship skill worth practising.
Which debate between friends would you happily reopen purely for the entertainment?
Recall a person joining your group's debate and making an unexpectedly good point.
A friendly argument breaks out over which shared memory happened first. How should we choose a winner?
Settle a harmless disagreement with a vote or let someone tell the best story?
